overall_assessment:
One material P2 adherence finding remains: NUM-ADH-CP36C-01. The two previous P2 source defects are corrected, and the current PostgreSQL positive now exercises their combined real lifecycle successfully. However, the new deliberately inconclusive provider-verification path loses its catalog error at the BFF boundary. Return this frozen package for a narrow transport-error correction before accepting every promised verification outcome. No new P1 authentication/tenant/data-loss defect, credential leak, SSRF, unbounded provider scan, network call inside a transaction, or architectural redesign was established. This recommendation concerns the bounded source correction; it is not final review, runtime recovery acceptance or whole-delivery acceptance.

Authority, scope and provenance: loaded the dedicated cp36c package/dispatch, its common bounded contract, governing TODO sections including frozen D-01..D-10 and module snapshot, the current channel module and relevant identity/inbox/audit/constitutional invariants, profile/effort/delivery-gate instructions and P1/P2/Rule-Spirit rubric. Routing-cp36c-adherence.json is GO, blocked=false, formal-reviewer, declared gpt-6.1-sol/max. Genesis is inapplicable; the active profile is Assurance / Security-Adversarial with NestJS, Prisma and PostgreSQL scope, plus read-only Docker validation-contract inspection. Inspected all eight allowed source/test files, the seven tracked exact-path diffs against API HEAD f134bd11449a553e6f57e66cdc8fc71032151060, and the untracked convergence helper directly. Read only necessary adjacent public controller/credential/attempt/lease/exception wiring and the expressly admitted Persons failure-classification excerpts. Recomputed the eight public source hashes using cp36c-source-before.sha256; all eight match. No source writes, tests, builds, runtime/provider/network calls, private dotenv/payload/operator-log access, Git mutations, goals, delegation or worktrees were performed. Only this raw result is written; root owns canonical records, classification and implementation authority.

Previous findings: NUM-ADH-CP36-01 is corrected in source by the exact nullable expected epoch at receipt-attempt-convergence.ts:8,14,22 and trusted type selection at channels.service.ts:336-337. OFICIAL uses null, while the Evolution caller at evolution.controller.ts:130 supplies only the numeric epoch derived from its current mapped channel. There is no generic null-or-numeric alternative. NUM-ADH-CP36B-01 is corrected by channels.service.ts:287 invoking the dedicated verificarNumeroVinculado operation, whose Meta implementation at meta.client.ts:137-157 revalidates the app/current scoped grant once and searches at most two scoped phone pages. confirmarNumero remains the selected-one-page operation at lines 127-133; onboarding selection is not silently broadened.

Behavioral evidence for those two corrections is substantive. The existing normal official BFF/PostgreSQL lifecycle still selects phone 987654321 on the second page with after=fixture-page-1 (number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:23-26,50-56), subscribes and receives an authenticated keyed receipt, and proves the persisted attempt has null epoch while the channel has zero epoch (77-87). Two administrative verify requests must return 200 (89-95). Postconditions preserve the same currentAttemptId, generation, completed attempt version, credential metadata, durable identity owner/current mapping and receipt (97-106). This is not a reordered first-page fixture or a mock success. The current log records this flow file green with 29 PostgreSQL tests. This supports bounded local behavioral resolution of both prior P2s; root must record their formal disposition and must not relabel the historical status-only RED as an observed ATTEMPT_STALE or PROVIDER_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND response.

Decision adherence — D-01: Adherent in the changed source. No new BU/tenant or ownership-transfer mechanism is added. Verification remains scoped by buId/type, locks the retained provider owner and rechecks the canonical phone inside the commit transaction (channels.service.ts:261-275,317-330). Evolution derives BU/channel from its durable provider-specific identity, not from message-supplied owner fields.

D-02: Preserved. Embedded Signup, SDK candidates, public capability and explicit operator selection remain unchanged. The new persisted-number lookup independently validates the configured app, is_valid, both WhatsApp scopes and their intersection on the requested WABA before fetching its phone edge (meta.client.ts:93-103,137-146,199-210). It does not trust an arbitrary SDK phone ID or a provider-supplied next URL.

D-03: Adherent at the changed convergence/lease/transaction locus. Pending promotion still uses exact attempt ID/generation/applicable epoch and increments version once; an exact CONNECTED/RECEIPT_VERIFIED attempt is accepted without another version write (receipt-attempt-convergence.ts:10-25). No nonce/code reuse, credential promotion, schema normalization or HTTP under a DB transaction is introduced. The existing channel reservation and commit fences retain one unexpired 45-second lease and currentAttemptId/generation/channel epoch. The public inconclusive-error mismatch is recorded separately rather than excused by these valid fences.

D-04: Preserved. The active credential is still resolved/decrypted for this exact channel and generation with the existing active AAD (channel-credential-resolver.ts:24-59); no global customer token or fallback is introduced. The adapter receives that explicit token and uses the app credential only for debug_token. The new tests compare safe credential identity/version metadata, not active token/envelope contents.

D-05: Partly adherent, with an unresolved exception at the promised visible/deterministic partial-failure outcome: NUM-ADH-CP36C-01. Authorization, registration, subscription and receipt remain separate; verify performs no provider mutation or callback takeover. Already subscribed official channels converge only with retained receipt evidence. Yet an authorized target beyond the bounded two-page search produces an internal MetaIndisponivelError that the BFF currently turns into a generic 500 without its catalog code.

D-06: Adherent in this source delta, without closing the runtime exception. The new helper does not accept null for Evolution. Connection-event readiness still requires open, ownNumberVerified, verifiedEpoch equal to the numeric current epoch and a durable receipt (evolution.controller.ts:121-130). Header authentication, exact instance mapping, identity -> BU -> channel lock order and generation/epoch re-read remain. The new PG tests prove completed-attempt verify/connecting/open/duplicate-open recovery and unchanged version/receipt/owner (flow:664-692), and reject cancelled, wrong-generation, wrong-epoch and null-epoch attempts with ATTEMPT_STALE and retained CONNECTING state (695-719). The already recorded D-06 temporary runtime exception remains pending until corrected-runtime recovery and the human proof are completed.

D-07: The observation/identity/CAS design is preserved; the new public error-envelope outcome has the explicit catalog exception in NUM-ADH-CP36C-01. Provider connection, own-number proof, receipt and registration remain separate. An inconclusive search does not mark a number absent in the database, fabricate online/offline state or converge an attempt. List remains DB-only (channels.controller.ts:27-39), owner remains durable, and network work is bounded. The missing error translation nevertheless prevents the promised distinction from reaching the caller as a catalogued result.

D-08: Preserved in this delta. No sender, message acceptance, Typebot ownership or timeline contract is changed. The convergence helper only operates after trusted caller receipt/identity checks; it neither inserts a message nor publishes a second receipt. The new recovery case retains exactly one keyed message. Existing cross-tenant, ownership, pre-identity, reauthorization, lease-stale and old-epoch negative harness in the allowed flow file is retained, including the existing pre-ingress realtime spy. This is preservation assessment, not a fresh reenactment of the earlier entire cutover audit.

D-09: Preserved. The patch does not change schema, dependencies, runtime configuration, operator data, hosting, Evolution digest, callback deployment or ingress. The supplied runner/evidence uses the declared validation namespace; no operator reset or live DB repair was performed by this reviewer. Local test-provider evidence is not real Meta OAuth/appliance/IN/OUT evidence. Railway, coexistence, history import, proactive conversation and continuous health remain outside the acceptance claim.

D-10: Consistent with the bounded frozen principal-checkout package and root's single-writer serialization. All eight hashes matched during this read-only review; no source writer was authorized by this reviewer. This is not a substitute for root's final source/pre-worker freshness attestation or a claim that an unrelated browser failure passed.

Module decision consistency: integrations-and-channels#invariants and its verify contract preserve adapter ownership, explicit scoped credentials, bounded pages and secret-free failures, but the deterministic public catalog requirement remains unsatisfied for the new inconclusive path (module lines 6-10,28; finding below). The channel recovery paragraph at module line 39 is faithfully represented by exact provider applicability and completed-version idempotency. project_constitution#system-invariants is preserved at BU/account grants, backend authority, transport separation and persistent history; no canonical decision is silently superseded. inbox-and-conversations#contrato-aprovado-da-timeline-da-inbox is Preserved: this patch does not change persisted timeline pagination, ordering, unread semantics or conversation identity. identity-and-tenancy#Autorização do cadastro de números is Preserved: ADMIN/session is checked before the operation and revalidated after provider HTTP; a caller cannot use null epoch, an SDK ID or a cursor to acquire another BU. audit-and-history#Cadastro e diagnóstico de canais is Preserved in the changed code: errors use constant safe text internally and audit metadata stays scoped; no token, QR, raw URL or payload sink is added. There is no approved supersession or waiver for the remaining catalog mismatch.

Security, atomicity and concurrency: ChannelsController checks ADMIN before parsing the type, derives an allowed channel type and revalidates the live session/user/grant (channels.controller.ts:84-91,107-113). Verify locks the managed current owner before BU/channel, performs provider I/O outside the transaction, and before writing rechecks currentAttemptId, generation, numeric channel epoch, lease token and expiry (channels.service.ts:263-275,285-308,318-323). Canonical phone claim and channel/attempt convergence share the final transaction; a false helper result throws there, rolling back connected/trust writes. Finally releases only the matching generation/epoch/token lease (344-345). Existing cancellation obtains a channel lease and rechecks the current attempt; stale/cancelled attempts are never accepted merely because a provider is open. Evolution verifies its private header timing-safely before mapping and derives currentAttemptId from the locked current channel. The helper intentionally relies on these trusted fenced callers for owner/BU provenance rather than duplicating an independent ownership resolver.

Meta security and budget: real adapter grant validation is once per persisted-number operation; wabaTargets intersects management and messaging granular targets. Each subsequent phone lookup is on the same WABA using the explicit channel token, fixed Graph host/version and redirect:error, with encoded path and URLSearchParams cursor handling (meta.client.ts:106-124,137-157,178-195). Provider next URLs are only continuation signals and are never followed. A nonempty string cursor over 512, a missing/non-string cursor paired with next, a cycle, or remaining pages after the second page causes a constant-text MetaIndisponivelError; no unbounded retry or mutation is added. One debug request plus at most two phone requests, each with a 10-second AbortSignal, gives at most three external calls and nominal 30 seconds of network budget within the existing 45-second lease. DB/session time can still consume the margin; the post-network and commit fences reject expired work rather than promising completion. The remaining finding is an application error-mapping defect, not a demonstrated credential leak or SSRF.

Performance position is acceptable for this correction: a helper CAS miss adds one primary-key-scoped read selecting only ID, under the existing channel transaction fence. There is no list fan-out, tenant-sized lookup, new index requirement or schema migration. The extra second phone page is a deliberate bounded verification cost; debugToken is not repeated for each page. Real-adapter tests at meta.client.spec.ts:125-193 invoke the actual adapter under a fetch stub and assert the exact three-call ceiling, fixed host, redirect policy, explicit auth, scoped target, exhaustion, budget, cycle and oversized cursor branches. E2E metaFake.providerCalls counts phone-page calls for this operation and omits a separate Graph debug-token call; it must not be reported as an actual Graph HTTP total. No fresh latency/SLO, capacity or PCV4 stress measurement is claimed; old PCV lane envelopes remain historical.

Elegance is acceptable: the single Channels-domain convergence helper gives both trusted callers one precise transition rule; explicit provider epoch applicability is clearer than a broad OR-null predicate or data normalization. A distinct persisted-number adapter operation preserves the different intent of selected-page onboarding confirmation. The small bounded loop is proportional to this approved recovery need, and the fixture changes mirror scoped bounded selection instead of returning every phone or bypassing the adapter. Structural soundness is mixed only because the new failure outcome is not translated at the existing transport boundary; a typed narrow mapping is preferable to a global catch-all, a new abstraction layer or a larger platform redesign.

Protection harness and evidence limits: the changed tests retain real Nest DI, BFF/session/CSRF/grants, signed receipts and PostgreSQL lifecycle state; only outgoing provider ports are doubled. The official postconditions and Evolution negative/rollback checks are behavior-relevant rather than assertion count alone. The added adapter tests exercise real production pagination/auth/URL-building code but stub fetch; they are not external provider proof. They check the exception class internally, which misses the BFF error-envelope defect. The cp36c log shows API lint/build, 141 unit and 288 PG tests green, 22 existing migrations, Web build and 28 unit green. At dispatch the browser was running; root subsequently reported terminal canonical all failure, and the named log records 46 browser passes plus one failure at the Persons invitation case. There is no current all-GREEN acceptance, no accepted fresh TQA outcome inferred, and this reviewer did not inspect/accept the actual pre-worker browser freshness attestation. A distinct final review is still required.

P1/P2 and Rule-Spirit hunt: one P2 public error-contract gap is established; no new P1 is demonstrated. The two prior P2 source causes are not reopened after their actual fixes. The patch does not swallow ATTEMPT_STALE, drop generation/epoch predicates, broaden null acceptance, revive cancelled attempts, bump completed versions gratuitously, trust arbitrary provider IDs/URLs, fall back to a global token, perform SQL repair, retry OAuth mutations blindly or reorder the selected fixture just to pass. Test counters are kept distinct from actual network proof, and failed/pending gates are not converted into pass artifacts. Existing test-after/mixed-process debt remains; cp36b's genuine functional RED is usable for the paging symptom but its status-only output does not identify the official catalog code or isolate the earlier epoch failure. The first cp36 unofficial RED has only excerpt/totals/before-hashes, not full raw stdout. This review neither reconstructs that stdout nor claims a new causal pre-fix RED.

Residual/debt boundaries: dependency audit exposure recorded in the package remains eight affected dependencies, one critical/six high/one moderate, including authenticated Multer DoS, restricted to the private OWNER/synthetic cohort with BLG-leadshug-runtime-dependency-security due before untrusted authenticated users. No new dependency audit or upgrade is claimed. The post-commit/pre-publication crash gap, no outbox, no automatic replay and no ordering promise remain recorded limits, not new architecture work. Real official OAuth/selected TEST resource/IN/OUT/recovery remains mandatory and unwaived. cp33 first unofficial human IN/OUT is historical accepted evidence; corrected-runtime recovery and a fresh human IN/OUT exchange remain pending. TODO remains active Pending; no production/continuous-health/general feature closure follows from API tests.

Separate browser classification, expressly admitted by root: Usuarios.tsx initializes novo.buId empty (24), fills it only after three asynchronous reads finish (28-38), submits that value (58-61), and enables Convidar without a loading/selected-BU guard (90-105). telas.spec.ts:338-348 fills/clicks immediately without selecting or waiting for Número. UsuariosService.exigirBusDaMantenedora rejects an empty/unknown BU before user creation (249-257). This is a concrete independent readiness race capable of producing HTTP 400 and no Ana row. The failing request body/catalog error was not captured, so it remains a source-supported hypothesis for the observed 400, not proof of its exact cause. No changed cp36c provider/convergence operation is invoked on that invitation path; this evidence does not establish a cp36c causal regression. recommended_path:
Root should integrate NUM-ADH-CP36C-01 for a serialized correction inside the existing approved D-05/D-07 deterministic-error contract. Preserve this immutable eight-file snapshot, its green API leaves and failed full-all result. After every current reader is terminal, admit only the necessary caller/test correction: map MetaIndisponivelError specifically to a fixed safe ServiceUnavailableException response with code META_INDISPONIVEL, while preserving all existing HttpException/auth/CAS failures and the lease finally block. Do not turn arbitrary programming/DB errors into provider errors or expose raw upstream text/URLs/tokens.

Add meaningful real BFF/Nest/PostgreSQL negative coverage for the deliberately inconclusive path, in addition to the actual adapter's existing budget/cursor tests: assert HTTP 503 and the exact catalog code; preserve channel observation/trust/status, current attempt/version, credential metadata, durable identity/current owner and receipt; prove the operation lease is cleared. Use an authentic bounded pre-fix failure where feasible and retain the historical evidence limits; do not rerun or reconstruct old RED solely to manufacture provenance. Refresh the new source freeze and required canonical validation plus affected independent TQA/adherence before a distinct final review. This reviewer performs or authorizes none of those edits.

The proposed separate Persons test concretization is reasonable as a future harness-only correction if root records its admission before writing and waits for all current readers to stop: explicitly choose the fixture-owned Número de QA through the existing Número select, register the real invitation POST response wait before clicking, assert actual 201, and retain Ana visibility, sector grant and cleanup assertions. Choosing the requested owned BU establishes a legitimate existing form precondition; it does not bypass backend validation or simulate invitation success. Do not add sleeps, retry-only passes, mocks, ignored 400s or remove the positive assertions. This is not proof that the observed failure was certainly BU_INVALIDA, and it does not resolve the underlying product readiness race for users; a separate product follow-up may be recorded under its own scope if root judges it necessary.

A future canonical browser leaf can supply new browser evidence for those future test bytes with a current pre-worker freshness attestation, followed by a fresh bounded technical TQA on that test delta and final root adjudication. The original canonical all stays failed in history; report leaf results individually rather than renaming that command successful. Such a browser rerun alone cannot clear the current API error-mapping P2. Whether already accepted API/Web leaves remain reusable depends on their exact unchanged source/build bindings; an API correction requires its own refreshed applicable validation. Neither this review nor a future one-test harness approval extends the current eight-file acceptance to unreviewed bytes.

Keep runtime/API-only operator update, corrected unofficial recovery plus new human exchange, and real official VAL-05 separate and mandatory. No runtime update, production/continuous-health claim, external recovery acceptance or whole-TODO closeout should rely on this report while the catalog P2, current required validation/reviews and external proof remain open. No broader architecture redesign, schema/dependency change or operational-data repair is recommended.

findings.title: [P2] Inconclusive persisted-number verification loses its public catalog error
findings.rationale:
Source-confirmed counterexample, not a request executed by this reviewer: take an authorized official channel with its exact current owner/credential and a persisted phone not present on the first two current WABA pages, where page two still returns a valid next cursor. The new method deliberately stops after one debug request plus two phone pages and throws MetaIndisponivelError at meta.client.ts:153. Malformed/oversized/cyclic cursor paths throw the same type at lines 121-122,150-157. This is the expected safe inconclusive branch of the new bounded contract, rather than resource-not-found or successful convergence.

That class extends plain Error and adds only code/detalhe (meta.client.ts:33-35); it is neither a Nest HttpException nor an HTTP error with statusCode. ChannelsService.verificar awaits it at channels.service.ts:287 and has only a finally lease release at 344-345, with no translation. ChannelsController.verificar simply returns that promise at channels.controller.ts:86-91. AppModule registers only the Prisma-specific BancoAtrasadoFilter (app.module.ts:39; banco-atrasado.filter.ts:19). The installed public Nest BaseExceptionFilter source, read only at node_modules/@nestjs/core/exceptions/base-exception-filter.js:16-17,34-46,62-64, sends this unknown Error as generic HTTP 500 with an Internal server error message and no code field. Therefore the class's internal META_INDISPONIVEL property never reaches the BFF caller.

Why now: cp36c newly establishes budget/cursor exhaustion as a normal deliberate verification outcome and explicitly promises a safe catalogued inconclusive error. The channel module's verify contract requires provider failures to map to application catalog codes (integrations-and-channels.md:28), under D-05/D-07's explicit recoverable failures and separate observations. The older generic Meta error plumbing predates this patch; this finding concerns the newly material bounded outcome at the changed verify locus, not a broad reopening of historically accepted integration architecture. Adapter unit tests at meta.client.spec.ts:173-193 assert only toBeInstanceOf(MetaIndisponivelError), and the green PG lifecycle covers a successful second page, so neither tests the actual failure envelope. No credential leakage, tenant bypass or persisted status mutation is demonstrated; the response is safe but fails its approved public error contract and hides a legitimate inconclusive result as an internal server failure.
findings.candidate_rule_id: D-05/D-07; integrations-and-channels explicit catalogued bounded verification outcomes
findings.suggested_action:
Recommend A: translate only the recognized MetaIndisponivelError at the existing verify application/transport boundary into HTTP 503 with the fixed safe catalog code META_INDISPONIVEL and a constant inconclusive/unavailable message. Keep the outgoing adapter/domain error separate from HTTP policy where practical. Preserve existing HttpException/auth/CAS exceptions, exact owner/currentAttempt/generation/epoch/receipt predicates, no network under transactions and the finally lease release. Add real BFF/Nest/PostgreSQL negative coverage that asserts status plus catalog code and proves unchanged credential/attempt version/identity/receipt/channel observations and released lease; retain the real adapter's exact request-budget and cursor tests. Effort small; risk low with a type-specific mapping; blast radius the verify caller and scoped test; maintenance low; no new query/network cost; elegance and structural soundness improve by completing the already owned boundary.

B: add a broad/global typed provider-error filter for every Meta consumer. It could be coherent under a separately admitted scope, but has larger blast radius and retest/maintenance burden and offers no performance advantage for this narrow correction; it is unnecessary here. C: leave generic HTTP 500. Zero implementation effort and no performance cost, but the new deliberate inconclusive outcome remains indistinguishable from a programming failure and violates the existing catalog contract; not recommended. Neither a blanket catch-all, a 200/null fallback, relaxed provider proof nor declaring the adapter unit green is a valid substitute. Root owns admission, classification, implementation and final disposition.
